outcome: The core conjecture (Sato-Tate for non-CM elliptic curves over Q) was already a theorem before 26 January 2024, via Clozel-Harris-Shepherd-Barron-Taylor (2008) and Barnet-Lamb-Geraghty-Harris-Taylor (2009/2011). Since then the only in-window movement on the generalisations is family-level or analogue work: Sato-Tate groups and, in some cases, the generalised equidistribution for specific families of higher-genus Jacobians (Goodson-Hoque 2024, Gallese-Goodson-Lombardo 2025, Emory-Goodson v2 2026), Sato-Tate-type laws for high-rank zeta functions of elliptic curves (Shi-Weng 2024/2025, not the L-function of E), a conditional function-field and rank-n consequence (Vladuts 2025), and a Kloosterman analogue over function fields (Fu-Lau-Li-Xi 2024). No in-window result proves Serre's generalised conjecture for abelian varieties of dimension at least 2 in general, and no in-window result addresses Katz's horizontal conjecture.
problem_asks: The bullet is 'Sato-Tate conjecture: also a number of related conjectures that are generalizations of the original conjecture'. Unpacked: (1) For an elliptic curve E over Q without complex multiplication, and each prime p of good reduction, define theta_p in [0, pi] by a_p = 2 sqrt(p) cos(theta_p) where a_p = p + 1 - #E(F_p); the angles are equidistributed with respect to the Sato-Tate measure (2/pi) sin^2(theta) d theta. Equivalently the Frobenius conjugacy classes equidistribute in SU(2). (2) 'A number of related conjectures that are generalizations of the original conjecture'. The bullet names none, so the record reads it as the set the literature attaches to the name, and the judging pass should check this reading against the January 2024 wording: (2a) the same statement for non-CM holomorphic newforms of weight >= 2 and for regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL2 over totally real or CM fields (Hilbert and Bianchi forms); (2b) Serre's generalised Sato-Tate conjecture: for an abelian variety or curve of dimension or genus g, normalised Frobenius classes equidistribute in its Sato-Tate group, a compact subgroup of USp(2g) (this requires both identifying the group and proving the equidistribution); (2c) joint or independent forms: for several non-isogenous curves or newforms, the angles are jointly equidistributed or statistically independent; (2d) Katz's horizontal Sato-Tate conjecture for Kloosterman sums (fix a, vary the prime p). Nearby but probably not part of the bullet: Lang-Trotter, Chebotarev-Sato-Tate, Drinfeld-module and function-field analogues.

events.what_happened: Michael Harris, in a 2008 Oxford seminar abstract, described a conditional argument: if a version of the stable trace formula became available, the same techniques would imply that the point counts of two non-isogenous elliptic curves over finite fields are statistically independent (joint form, 2c). Wikipedia reports the same conditional result. The seminar abstract was seen in search results only and was not opened.
events.delivers: Conditional on an unproven version of the stable trace formula, independence of Frobenius data for two non-isogenous non-CM elliptic curves. The abstract says the analogous statements for three or more non-isogenous curves are out of reach.
events.remains: Unconditional joint equidistribution or independence for any pair (2c); all cases with three or more curves (2c); the conditional hypothesis itself.
events.doubts: Conditional on a trace formula that the abstract describes as 'soon to be available'. The record does not show whether that hypothesis was later established; Wikipedia credits Harris and Sug Woo Shin with resolving trace-formula issues but does not say which ones.
events.direction: Consistent with the joint form of the conjecture: it predicts and conditionally proves independence of the two Frobenius distributions.

events.what_happened: Clozel, Harris, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor published a proof of the Sato-Tate conjecture for elliptic curves over totally real fields, with an extra hypothesis of multiplicative reduction at some prime, in three papers in 2008. Harris, Shepherd-Barron and Taylor (2010, Invent. Math.) are cited alongside it on the Wikipedia article. The original papers were not opened; the account comes from the Wikipedia article.
events.delivers: Sato-Tate for elliptic curves over totally real fields that have multiplicative reduction at some prime, which covers the original conjecture over Q only in the cases meeting that hypothesis (per Wikipedia).
events.remains: Elliptic curves over totally real fields without multiplicative reduction (removed by the 2009-2011 papers below); all higher-dimensional and automorphic generalisations (2a)-(2d).

checked_by.qualification: Authors; established specialists in automorphic forms and Galois representations
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the proof in three papers in 2008 (per Wikipedia)

events.doubts: The Wikipedia article gives the first proof as 2008 in one place and as 2011 in its infobox and body; the two dates reflect the conditional and unconditional steps and are not a dispute about priority.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for the cases proved.

events.what_happened: Tom Barnet-Lamb, David Geraghty, Michael Harris and Richard Taylor, 'A family of Calabi-Yau varieties and potential automorphy II', Publ. RIMS Kyoto 47 (2011) 29-98. The EMS Press page gives a submission date of 6 July 2009 (a journal-submission date; the arXiv posting date was not confirmed). The abstract says all symmetric powers of any non-CM holomorphic cuspidal elliptic newform of weight greater than one are potentially cuspidal automorphic, 'This in turns proves the Sato-Tate conjecture for such forms', and that Sato-Tate can now be proved for any elliptic curve over a totally real field.

events.delivers: The original Sato-Tate conjecture for non-CM elliptic curves over Q (weight > 1 newforms, via the symmetric-power automorphy result), and for elliptic curves over any totally real field, with no extra multiplicative-reduction hypothesis (per the abstract and the Wikipedia article). It also covers non-CM holomorphic newforms of weight greater than one.
events.remains: Generalisations (2b)-(2d): Serre's conjecture for abelian varieties of dimension >= 2, joint forms, Katz's horizontal Kloosterman conjecture.

events.remains: Equidistribution for each group, and the conjecture for most abelian surfaces (2b).

events.what_happened: Noah Taylor, 'Sato-Tate distributions on abelian surfaces', arXiv 1808.00243 (first version 1 August 2018; v2 4 July 2019). Proves a few new cases of Sato-Tate for abelian surfaces using an automorphy theorem of Allen et al., and gives asymptotics and optimal bounds for the trace of Frobenius in the unproven cases. The arXiv abstract was opened. A Trans. AMS 373 (2020) listing appeared in search results but was not opened.
events.revisions: v1 1 Aug 2018; v2 4 Jul 2019; Trans. AMS 373 (2020) per search listing.
events.delivers: Sato-Tate for a few new cases of abelian surfaces (2b). Where it does not settle the distribution, it gives bounds: for a positive proportion of primes, a_v < -2/3 + eps and a_v > 2/3 - eps (search snippet of the Trans. AMS version).
events.remains: The generic case, where the endomorphism ring is Z (per search snippet), and most of 2b.
events.direction: Confirms the generalised conjecture for the new cases; gives bounds elsewhere.

events.what_happened: Yang-Hui He, Kyu-Hwan Lee and Thomas Oliver, 'Machine-learning the Sato-Tate conjecture', arXiv 2010.01213 (2 October 2020); J. Symb. Comput. 111 (2022) 61-72. A Bayesian classifier and PCA distinguish Sato-Tate groups for hyperelliptic curves from a few Euler factors, with 99-100% reported accuracy, and the observations are said to agree with the conjecture for low-genus curves.
events.revisions: v1 2 Oct 2020; v2 later; JSC 111 (2022).

events.remains: Everything in the problem statement; this is numerical support only.

events.what_happened: Alexandra Hoey, Jonas Iskander, Steven Jin and Fernando Trejos Suarez, 'An unconditional explicit bound on the error term in the Sato-Tate conjecture', arXiv 2108.03520 (7 August 2021; v3 25 January 2022). For holomorphic newforms of even weight k >= 2, level N, no CM, trivial nebentypus, they give an unconditional explicit bound on |proportion of p <= x with theta_p in I, minus mu_ST(I)|, of the form 58.1 log((k-1)N log x)/sqrt(log x), for forms from elliptic curves over Q or of squarefree level (per the abstract). Uses Newton and Thorne.
events.revisions: v1 7 Aug 2021; v3 25 Jan 2022 (minor changes).
events.delivers: A quantitative (explicit error term) form of Sato-Tate for a restricted class: non-CM newforms of weight at least 2 that come from elliptic curves over Q or have squarefree level. It is an analogue of the original statement, not a new case of the distribution itself, since the qualitative result was already known for these forms.
events.remains: Generalisations (2b)-(2d) and the unrestricted newform class in the quantitative form.
events.direction: Quantitative strengthening for a restricted class; consistent with the conjecture.

Prove the generalised conjecture for these two families of hyperelliptic Jacobians of arbitrarily high genus (p odd prime). Seen in search snippets only.
events.delivers: Generalised Sato-Tate (2b) for the Jacobians of y^2 = x^p - 1 and y^2 = x^{2p} - 1, p an odd prime (per search summary; their Jacobians are CM per that summary).
events.remains: All other families and the general case (2b).

events.what_happened: Melissa Emory and Heidi Goodson, 'Nondegeneracy and Sato-Tate distributions of two families of Jacobian varieties', arXiv 2401.06208 (v1 11 January 2024, which predates the frozen revision by fifteen days; v2 6 January 2026, to appear in Research in Number Theory, specialises to c = 1). The abstract was opened. Studies y^2 = x^{2^m} - 1 and y^2 = x^{2^d + 1} - x over Q: proves nondegeneracy via Hodge groups, determines the Sato-Tate groups (generators of component groups), and computes moment statistics to compare with the equidistribution the generalised conjecture predicts.
events.revisions: v1 11 Jan 2024 (c arbitrary nonzero rational); v2 6 Jan 2026 (c = 1 only; Research in Number Theory version).
events.delivers: Determination of the Sato-Tate groups (2b) for two families of Jacobians over Q, with nondegeneracy. The equidistribution itself is not established: it is checked numerically via moments and stated as the predicted behaviour.
events.remains: Equidistribution (2b) for these families, which the abstract presents as predicted rather than proved; the general case.
events.doubts: The abstract presents the equidistribution as consistent with moment statistics, not as a theorem. The v1 and v2 statements differ (general c versus c = 1), so the scope narrowed between versions.
events.direction: Group determination consistent with the generalised conjecture; equidistribution predicted but not proved.

events.what_happened: Lei Fu, Yuk-Kam Lau, Wen-Ching Winnie Li and Ping Xi, 'Equidistribution of Kloosterman sums over function fields', arXiv 2406.10106 (submitted 14 June 2024; v2 24 November 2025), published IMRN 2025 (rnaf229). The abstract was opened. Proves a Sato-Tate distribution for Kloosterman sums over function fields, with explicit error terms, when the places vary in arithmetic progressions or short intervals, and a joint Sato-Tate distribution for two exponential sums.
events.revisions: v1 14 Jun 2024; v2 24 Nov 2025; IMRN 2025 rnaf229 (search result).
events.delivers: A function-field analogue of Sato-Tate for Kloosterman sums, with the places restricted to arithmetic progressions or short intervals, and a joint version for two sums. Function-field results are analogues in the sense of section 2.1; they do not settle the classical conjecture over Q.
events.remains: The classical statement over Q (Katz's horizontal conjecture for Kloosterman sums over Z is untouched by this function-field result); the classical bullet's statement.

events.what_happened: Zhan Shi and Lin Weng, 'Murmurations and Sato-Tate conjectures for high rank zetas of elliptic curves', arXiv 2410.04952 (first submitted 7 October 2024; single version). Abstract (opened): 'For elliptic curves over rationals, there are a well-known conjecture of Sato-Tate and a new computational guided murmuration phenomenon ... we show that both the murmurations and the Sato-Tate conjecture stand equally well for non-abelian high rank zeta functions of the p-reductions of elliptic curves over rationals.'
events.revisions: v1 7 Oct 2024 only (per arXiv page).
events.delivers: Per the abstract, a Sato-Tate-type statement for non-abelian high-rank zeta functions of the reductions of elliptic curves over Q. This is an analogue (a different zeta function, not the L-function of E in the original conjecture), so per section 2.1 it does not settle the bullet. The theorem statement was not visible in the abstract.
events.remains: The original conjecture for the L-function of E (the abelian zeta case); the generalised conjecture (2a)-(2d) is not addressed by the abstract.
events.doubts: Only the abstract and page were read; the proof was not read. The abstract's wording ('stand equally well') does not state a theorem. No published review or citing paper was found in searches; a citation search was not done.
events.direction: Analogue result: a Sato-Tate-type law for a different class of zeta functions; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Zhan Shi and Lin Weng, 'Murmurations and Sato-Tate conjectures for high rank zetas of elliptic curves II: beyond Riemann hypothesis', arXiv 2501.10220 (first submitted 17 January 2025; v2 21 January 2025). Per the arXiv page read via fetch (summarised, not verbatim): a new approach to murmurations and Sato-Tate laws for higher-rank zetas of elliptic curves; the rank-n Sato-Tate law 'can be established' without the Riemann hypothesis for the a-invariant in rank n > 2, using stronger asymptotic bounds.
events.delivers: Per the abstract as summarised, a rank-n Sato-Tate law for higher-rank zetas of elliptic curves. An analogue of the bullet's conjecture, not the L-function of E; the rank-n law is conditional on nothing (per the abstract) but its proof was not read.
events.remains: The original conjecture for E over Q; the generalised conjecture (2a)-(2d).
events.doubts: Read from the abstract only; the proof was not read. Its relation to Part I (same authors, Oct 2024) and to the earlier Riemann-hypothesis dependence is not checked. No review or citing paper was found in searches.
events.direction: Analogue result: a rank-n Sato-Tate law for zetas, not for the L-function of E.

events.what_happened: Heidi Goodson and Rezwan Hoque, 'Sato-Tate groups and distributions of y^l = x(x^l - 1)', arXiv 2412.02522 (submitted 3 December 2024; v2 26 August 2025, described as the final version accepted to Acta Arithmetica). The arXiv HTML was opened. Theorem 3.4: the Sato-Tate group of Jac(C_l) for each prime l >= 3 is <U(1)^g, gamma>, with g = l(l-1)/2 and gamma a block-signed permutation matrix; the component group is cyclic of order l(l-1). The authors state that the generalised Sato-Tate conjecture 'is known to be true for this family', relying on CM results of Johansson and on Banaszak-Kedlaya for nondegenerate varieties. Numerical a1-moments are computed for primes p < 2^22 with p = 1 mod 25.
events.revisions: v1 3 Dec 2024; v2 26 Aug 2025 (accepted Acta Arithmetica per the abstract page).
events.delivers: For every prime l >= 3, the full Sato-Tate group of the Jacobian of y^l = x(x^l - 1), and, per the authors, the equidistribution (generalised Sato-Tate, 2b) for this one-parameter family of genus l(l-1)/2. Restricted to this family; each prime l gives a separate genus.
events.remains: Other families of Jacobians, the general Serre conjecture for abelian varieties (2b), and the original elliptic-curve statement, which is already known.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication, per the arXiv comment as read (not confirmed by a journal page)

events.doubts: The equidistribution is presented as known via earlier CM results rather than proved here; whether those results apply to this family as stated is a claim the judging pass should check in the body of the paper. The numerical moments are checks, not proofs. No citing review was found.
events.direction: Consistent with the generalised conjecture for the family; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Andrea Gallese, Heidi Goodson and Davide Lombardo, 'Monodromy groups and exceptional Hodge classes, II: Sato-Tate groups', arXiv 2507.02535 (submitted 3 July 2025; single version). The HTML v1 was opened (first c. 100,000 of about 190,000 characters). Computes the Sato-Tate group of J_m, the Jacobian of y^2 = x^m + 1 over Q, for fixed m >= 3, gives an algorithm for ST(J_m) for any m, describes Sato-Tate groups for general abelian varieties, and extends a Gross-Koblitz formula. Authors state that the algebraic Sato-Tate and Mumford-Tate conjectures are known for these varieties and that the consequences for exceptional Hodge classes are unconditional.
events.revisions: v1 3 Jul 2025 only.
events.delivers: The Sato-Tate group (the target group of 2b) of J_m for each m >= 3, computed by an algorithm. It does not prove the equidistribution statement for J_m; the paper cites prior work proving the generalised conjecture for abelian varieties with potential CM, which would cover J_m if they are of CM type, but the authors do not draw that conclusion for J_m in the part read.
events.remains: Equidistribution for J_m (2b) as an explicit result in this paper; the general case.
events.doubts: The equidistribution for J_m is not proved in this paper. The first 100,000 characters were read; the last 89,595 were not, so any later statement in the body is not checked. No review or citing paper was found.
events.direction: Group-level computation consistent with the generalised conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: A. Anas Chentouf, Catherine Cossaboom, Samuel Goldberg and Jack B. Miller, 'Patterns of primes in joint Sato-Tate distributions', arXiv 2308.06632 (12 August 2023), J. Number Theory (dated 23 April 2024 by sugaku.net). Abstract (opened): for two non-CM holomorphic newforms f1, f2 of weight at least 2 with trivial nebentypus, if f1 is not a character twist of f2, there are infinitely many bounded gaps between primes p with theta_1(p) in I_1 and theta_2(p) in I_2; also a common generalisation with Green-Tao.
events.revisions: v1 12 Aug 2023; JNT 2024 (search result).
events.delivers: A statement about joint Sato-Tate distributions of two newforms, namely bounded gaps between primes landing in given joint intervals, under the non-twist condition (2c). It is a pattern result about primes, not an equidistribution or independence result.
events.remains: Joint equidistribution or independence of the two angles (2c); the twist case is excluded.
events.direction: Pattern result about joint distributions; not a settlement of (2c).

events.what_happened: George Boxer, Frank Calegari, Toby Gee, James Newton and Jack Thorne, 'The Ramanujan and Sato-Tate conjectures for Bianchi modular forms', arXiv 2309.15880 (first submitted 27 September 2023; v3 27 March 2025), published Forum of Mathematics, Pi 13 (2025), e10 (received 27 Sep 2023, accepted 27 Oct 2024, per the journal record in search results). Abstract (opened): 'We prove the Ramanujan and Sato-Tate conjectures for Bianchi modular forms of weight at least 2', extended to all regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL2 over any CM field of parallel weight. The method is a new potential automorphy theorem for symmetric powers of 2-dimensional compatible systems of parallel weight. The authors say Kojiro Matsumoto later proved more general results of this type (per a search snippet of a talk; the Matsumoto paper was not found).
events.revisions: v1 27 Sep 2023; v2 accepted version; v3 27 Mar 2025; Forum Math Pi 13 (2025) e10 (search result).
events.delivers: Sato-Tate (2a) for regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL2 of parallel weight over any CM field (including Bianchi forms of weight >= 2). Restrictions per the abstract: parallel weight; CM fields. Not covered by the abstract: non-parallel weight; number fields that are neither totally real nor CM; higher-dimensional abelian varieties (2b).
events.remains: Non-parallel weight over CM fields; general number fields outside the totally real and CM cases; the higher-dimensional forms (2b)-(2d).

events.what_happened: Yang-Hui He, Kyu-Hwan Lee, Thomas Oliver and Alexey Pozdnyakov, 'Murmurations: a case study in AI-assisted mathematics', arXiv 2603.09680 (submitted 10 March 2026). Abstract (opened): murmurations are a new phenomenon in arithmetic, found experimentally in averages over large arithmetic datasets; 'murmurations can be detected and analyzed using standard interpretability tools from machine learning'; they encode information about Frobenius traces and connect to the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture and random matrix theory. The page does not discuss Sato-Tate.

events.delivers: Nothing on Sato-Tate. It is a different phenomenon (rank-correlated averages of Frobenius traces), with the Sato-Tate measure appearing only as a background histogram reference in the slides of a related talk (search snippet). It does not bear on any clause of problem_asks (section 2.1).
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the record shows no result on the conjecture or its generalisations.
events.direction: Not about the problem; recorded as a discounted event.

Abstract (opened, paraphrased by fetch): conjectures a universal leading profile for root-number-weighted averages of normalised Hecke coefficients at p^k/X; proves it for each fixed k, for weight 2 newforms of squarefree level under conditions, extending Zubrilina (prime case) and Kundu-Muller (square case).

summary: Opened sources (arXiv abstracts or HTML, journal pages where reachable, and Wikipedia) establish the following. The original conjecture for non-CM elliptic curves over Q is a theorem: Clozel-Harris-Shepherd-Barron-Taylor (2008, with a multiplicative-reduction hypothesis) and Barnet-Lamb-Geraghty-Harris-Taylor (2009 submission, Publ. RIMS 2011; abstract opened) remove it, and Barnet-Lamb-Gee-Geraghty (Dec 2009, JAMS 2011; abstract opened) extend it to Hilbert modular forms. Wikipedia gives 2011 as the completion date and 2008 as the first proof; the record uses the dates of the papers. The in-window period (since 26 January 2024) contains no result that proves a clause of the generalisations in general: the events are (a) family-level determinations of Sato-Tate groups or generalised equidistribution for specific families of higher-genus Jacobians (Goodson-Hoque, arXiv 2412.02522, Dec 2024, where the equidistribution is stated as known via earlier CM results; Gallese-Goodson-Lombardo part II, arXiv 2507.02535, July 2025, which computes the group only; Emory-Goodson v1 11 Jan 2024 and v2 Jan 2026, where equidistribution is only checked numerically), (b) Sato-Tate-type laws for high-rank zetas of elliptic curves that are analogues of the L-function of E (Shi-Weng, arXiv 2410.04952 Oct 2024 and 2501.10220 Jan 2025; read from abstracts only), (c) a conditional consequence for quadratic residues (Vladuts, Sept 2025), and (d) a function-field analogue (Fu-Lau-Li-Xi, June 2024, IMRN 2025). The AI search found no AI-credited result on the Sato-Tate conjecture or its generalisations. The closest AI-related items are the He-Lee-Oliver machine-learning classifier (2020; empirical, no named system) and the 2026 murmurations papers (He-Lee-Oliver-Pozdnyakov, March 2026; Hua-Mok, Sept 2026), which concern different phenomena. Other AI-credited 2026 papers that surfaced (Szpiro bounds, Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds with an LLM disclosure, elliptic matroids, regular Diophantine triples) concern other problems; none mentions Sato-Tate on the page read. The Murmurations paper title says 'AI-assisted' but the abstract names no system. Close calls: (i) whether the Goodson-Hoque equidistribution is a new result or a corollary of earlier CM work the authors cite; (ii) whether the Shi-Weng zeta results count as generalisations of the bullet (they are analogues in the sense of section 2.1, so the record treats them as not settling the bullet); (iii) whether Gallese-Goodson-Lombardo part II settles equidistribution for J_m (the text read says no, the last 89,595 characters were not read). Searches for any in-window proof of Serre's generalised conjecture for abelian varieties of dimension at least 2 found none; the best in-window items are family-level or conditional.
competing_reading: The strongest case that something settled a generalisation in-window is Goodson-Hoque (arXiv 2412.02522): for every prime l >= 3 it determines the full Sato-Tate group of the Jacobian of y^l = x(x^l - 1) (genus l(l-1)/2, unbounded) and states the generalised equidistribution as known for the family. Read that way, it is a new infinite family of generalised Sato-Tate cases, and the in-window count is nonzero. The strongest case against counting it: the equidistribution is attributed to earlier CM results (Johansson; Banaszak-Kedlaya) rather than proved there, and the family is one parameter. Shi-Weng could be read as Sato-Tate-type theorems that generalise the bullet's 'related conjectures', if the bullet is taken to include Sato-Tate for zeta functions of higher rank. Against that, the zetas are not the L-function of E. Finally, the strongest case that nothing happened in-window at all is that every generalisation remains open in general and the in-window items are analogues, family-level, conditional or numerical.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The January 2024 wording and linked targets of the bullet, to know which generalisations the bullet names; the Wikipedia List of unsolved problems in mathematics was not opened. (2) The body of Goodson-Hoque (arXiv 2412.02522) and the last 89,595 characters of Gallese-Goodson-Lombardo part II, to see whether the equidistribution is proved in the paper or cited from elsewhere, and which result is cited. (3) The full text of Shi-Weng part I and II to see the theorem statements and whether the zeta results have the L-function of E as a special case. (4) A citation search (Google Scholar or zbMATH) for Goodson-Hoque, Emory-Goodson, Gallese-Goodson-Lombardo, Shi-Weng and Vladuts, to see whether any later paper calls the generalised conjecture open for these families or cites them as settling it. (5) The Matsumoto work referred to in Boxer et al., which was not located. (6) A Mathlib or formal-conjectures check, which was not reached (the DeepMind formal-conjectures repository was checked only at the root).
